Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ZenoHealth: Integration sprint owners & network gate

Hi Mark / Priya —

Thanks for the kickoff yesterday. To keep the private deployment sprint tight, we want to lock the network gate (VPC peering + private endpoints) before we schedule appliance shipment and installer windows.

Quick ask: can you confirm the Zeno network owners and provide a primary contact for the infra team? Once we have the contact we’ll run a short architecture review (30–45m) and surface any constraints that affect the on-prem package (appliance vs. containerized install).

I’ve attached our network checklist and the on-prem install matrix for your network team's reference. Proposed next steps:
- Zeno provides infra contact + CIDR ranges for peering (by Wed 21 Apr)
- Redwood schedules network review (45m) and shares routing/endpoint diagrams
- Post-review: agree on NAT/egress policy and cert provisioning timeline

Owners from our side: Monica (network runbook + peering config), Vivek (security/compliance + KMS integration), PrioM (on-prem install lead). I’ll coordinate the calendar.

Are mornings (10–11am PT) on Tue/Wed good for you for the technical review?

Thanks,
Aisha
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
Attachments: Zeno_network_checklist_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), onprem_install_matrix_v2.pdf (doc)
From: Mark Reynolds <mark.reynolds@zenohealth.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: infra-team@zenohealth.com, Priya Kapoor <priya.kapoor@zenohealth.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ZenoHealth: Integration sprint owners & network gate

Thanks Aisha —

Apologies for the slow reply, we were consolidating internal owners. Primary contact will be Priya (cc’d). Our infra alias (infra-team@zenohealth.com) is the best channel for config artifacts.

Notes from our side:
- CIDR plan: corp 10.10.0.0/16 (private), services 10.20.0.0/16
- We prefer VPC peering where possible; if private endpoints are used we need to route egress through our outbound proxy (envoy) for traffic inspection
- We have an internal change freeze window on 2027-04-28 -> 2027-05-02 (cannot schedule appliance installs during that week)

Priya — can your team share a list of IPs that Redwood should expect to see as source during the peering (esp. for health checks + KV cache syncing)? Also confirm whether you require mutual TLS for peered traffic or if IP allowlisting is acceptable.

Mark
Director, Infrastructure | ZenoHealth

Aisha / team —

I’ll take lead on the peering config and baseline routing. Action items I’ll own and will bring to the network review:
- Draft peering route table and security groups (initial draft by Wed 21 Apr EOD)
- Minimal IP set for health checks and runtime egress (need Zeno to confirm proxy IPs)
- Certificate flow for private endpoints (if mTLS is requested we’ll need cert signing timeline from Zeno KMS)

Vivek — can you prepare the compliance checklist (SOC2 section + data residency notes) and confirm whether any telemetry needs to be scrubbed before it leaves Zeno’s network?

I’ll send a calendar invite for Thu 21 Apr 10:30–11:15 PT for the architecture review — that avoids their change freeze and gives time to iterate on the initial draft.

Monica
Implementation Lead, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

Hi all — following up from the infra inbox.

We can confirm the following and have attached our initial network diagram to the infra thread.
- Source IPs for health checks: 52.23.101.12, 52.23.101.13, 34.78.210.9
- We require mTLS for endpoints that accept customer-provided keys. For peering and internal service-to-service traffic, IP allowlisting is fine but we prefer mutual TLS for any externally-terminating private endpoints
- We’ll provide a short window next week for cert signing (we need the CA CSR two business days prior)

The Thu 21 Apr 10:30–11:15 PT architecture review works for our infra lead. Please send the calendar invite and I’ll make sure the right engineer is there.

Thanks,
